1.note: The author is using the time reference **At that time** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event. Alternate translation: [And it happened]

1.q: שָׁלַ֡ח מְרֹדַ֣ךְ בַּ֠לְאֲדָן בֶּֽן־בַּלְאֲדָ֧ן מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֛ל סְפָרִ֥ים וּ⁠מִנְחָ֖ה אֶל־חִזְקִיָּ֑הוּ וַ⁠יִּשְׁמַ֕ע כִּ֥י חָלָ֖ה וַֽ⁠יֶּחֱזָֽק
1.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [since Merodach-Baladan, the son of Baladan, the king of Babylon, had heard that Hezekiah was sick, he sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah]

Some ancient manuscripts read “Merodach Baladan.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts and the parallel passage in 2 Kings 20:12 read “Berodach Baladan.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.
See how you translated the similar expression in 37:14. Alternate translation: [a letter]

2.note: Some ancient manuscripts read “And Hezekiah rejoiced upon them.” The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts and the parallel passage in 2 Kings 20:13 read “And Hezekiah listened to them.” If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.
Alternate translation: [and everything that was in his treasuries]

2.q: לֹֽא־הָיָ֣ה דָבָ֗ר אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹֽא־הֶרְאָ֧⁠ם חִזְקִיָּ֛הוּ בְּ⁠בֵית֖⁠וֹ וּ⁠בְ⁠כָל־מֶמְשַׁלְתּֽ⁠וֹ
2.note: This is a double negative, consisting of two instances of the negative particle **not**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [Hezekiah showed them everything in his palace and in his realm]

4.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 39:2. Alternate translation: [I showed them everything in my treasuries]

5.note: Isaiah is using the term **word** to represent what Yahweh said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Hear a message from Yahweh]

6.q: הִנֵּה֮ יָמִ֣ים בָּאִים֒ וְ⁠נִשָּׂ֣א ׀ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ⁠בֵיתֶ֗⁠ךָ וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָצְר֧וּ אֲבֹתֶ֛י⁠ךָ עַד־הַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה בָּבֶ֑ל לֹֽא־יִוָּתֵ֥ר דָּבָ֖ר אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה
6.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh says that behold, days are coming when all that is in your house and that your fathers have stored up to this day will be carried away to Babylon. A thing will not be left]
Yahweh uses the word **Behold** here to draw attention to the important announcement that follows. Alternate translation: [Hear me tell you]
Isaiah is using the term **days** to refer to a specific time in the future. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a time is coming]

6.q: וְ⁠נִשָּׂ֣א ׀ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּ⁠בֵיתֶ֗⁠ךָ וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָצְר֧וּ אֲבֹתֶ֛י⁠ךָ עַד־הַ⁠יּ֥וֹם הַ⁠זֶּ֖ה בָּבֶ֑ל
6.note: The expression **will be carried away** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that would be natural in your language. Alternate translation: [when soldiers will carry away to Babylon everything that {is} in your house and that your fathers have stored up to this day]
Isaiah is using the term **fathers** to mean “ancestors.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [your forebears] or [your forefathers]

7.q: וּ⁠מִ⁠בָּנֶ֜י⁠ךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵצְא֧וּ מִמְּ⁠ךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תּוֹלִ֖יד יִקָּ֑חוּ וְ⁠הָיוּ֙ סָרִיסִ֔ים בְּ⁠הֵיכַ֖ל מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל
7.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh also says that soldiers will take away some of your sons who will come forth from you, whom you will beget, and those sons will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon]

7.q: וּ⁠מִ⁠בָּנֶ֜י⁠ךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵצְא֧וּ מִמְּ⁠ךָ֛ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תּוֹלִ֖יד יִקָּ֑חוּ
7.note: Isaiah is speaking as if the future descendants of Hezekiah were actually his **sons**. Alternate translation: [some of the men of later generations who will descend from you, whose ancestor you will be]

These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [, some of your actual biological descendants]

8.note: Hezekiah does not mean that the content of this message from Yahweh is objectively **good**. He means that he accepts and submits to what Yahweh has decided. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. The UST models one way to do that.

By **For he said**, Isaiah probably means that Hezekiah said it to himself. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [For he thought to himself]

If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **peace** and **stability**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [For my kingdom will be peaceful and stable in my days]
